title: Cap and evict unbounded state.posts and SWR history cache
description:
## Problem
state.posts and the SWR channel-history cache grow unbounded. applyIncomingPost adds posts for any channel that has ever been loaded, with no eviction. mutateChannelHistory/appends forever to each channel's SWR-cached ChannelHistoryData. No SWRConfig cache provider is configured, so SWR's default global Map cache has no size limit.

## Root Cause
- utils/state.ts applyIncomingPost adds to state.posts for any loaded channel, never removes
- useMainViewEvents.ts addPostToHistory appends to SWR cache indefinitely
- No SWRConfig with custom cache provider/eviction anywhere
- Worker's historyCache.ts has bounded LRU (20 entries, 10min TTL) but main thread has no equivalent

## Solution
1. Add per-channel post cap in state.posts (e.g. keep last 500 posts per channel when not focused)
2. Configure SWR with a custom cache provider that has size limits, or manually prune old entries
3. Clean up chatViewStates when chat tabs are closed (currently never deleted)
4. Add eviction logic when channels are unselected or tabs are closed

## Acceptance Criteria
- state.posts is capped per channel
- SWR cache has bounded size
- chatViewStates is cleaned up on tab close
- No memory growth over extended sessions with multiple channels
notes:
Implemented:
1. utils/state.ts: added MAX_RESIDENT_POSTS_PER_CHANNEL=500 cap. addPost() trims oldest postOrder/posts entries for the standalone channel once it exceeds the cap (trimResidentPosts). applyIncomingPost()'s background-channel branch trims oldest-by-create_at posts via trimResidentBackgroundPosts. This bounds per-channel memory growth even for a single channel left open indefinitely.
2. Added evictInactiveChannelPosts(state, activeChannelIds) - removes all posts for channels no longer referenced by any open tab or the standalone selection.
3. MainViewApp.tsx handleCloseChatTab: when the closed tab was the last reference to a channel, calls evictInactiveChannelPosts, chatWorkspaceActions.forgetView(channelId), and swrCache.delete(unstable_serialize(key)) to drop the SWR history cache entry (SWR's default cache has no size limit).
4. chatWorkspaceStore.ts: added forgetView(viewId) action to clean up chatViewStates (draft/reply/edit state) on tab close - previously grew forever for every channel ever opened.

Tests added in state.test.ts (resident post cap + evictInactiveChannelPosts describe blocks) and chatWorkspaceStore.test.ts (forgetView tests). Updated a brittle exact-source-match test in MainViewApp.test.ts that broke due to the handleCloseChatTab changes.

All 328 tests pass, typecheck clean, biome clean.

Scope note: loadMoreMessages (explicit user-initiated pagination) is intentionally NOT capped since it's bounded by user action, not unbounded background accumulation.
close_reason: Implemented bounded post retention (per-channel cap + eviction on tab close) and SWR cache cleanup on tab close. See notes for details.

title: Tabbed chats never load newer messages (stale history cache)

Tests added in state.test.ts, MainViewApp.test.ts, new useMainViewEvents.test.ts. Full suite 249 pass, typecheck clean, biome clean on changed files.

title: Re-virtualize MuiMessageTimeline to prevent unbounded DOM growth
description:
## Problem
MuiMessageTimeline renders every message as a permanent DOM node with a dedicated ResizeObserver. The @mui/x-chat-headless MessageList.Root uses StaticMessageListView which maps over all items without windowing. With two chat tabs open over time, this causes unbounded DOM growth contributing to 6GB RAM usage.

## Root Cause
- node_modules/@mui/x-chat-headless/message-list/MessageListRoot.js uses StaticMessageListView
- StaticMessageListView does itemIds.map() mounting a real div + ResizeObserver for every message
- No virtualization despite estimatedItemSize prop (only used for scroll math)
- Codebase has a virtualized MessageTimeline.tsx using @tanstack/react-virtual but it's dead code

## Solution
Replace MessageList.Root in MuiMessageTimeline with a virtualized list using @tanstack/react-virtual. Keep MUI Chat components (MessageGroup, Message.Root, etc.) for individual message rendering. Handle scroll-to-bottom, load-more, and date dividers manually.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Timeline renders only visible messages + overscan buffer
- Scroll-to-bottom works correctly
- Load-more (onReachTop) triggers when scrolling to top
- Date dividers render correctly
- No visual regression in message layout
notes:
Re-scoped after antimatter-ojb: state.posts is now capped at 500 resident posts per channel (MAX_RESIDENT_POSTS_PER_CHANNEL in utils/state.ts), so MuiMessageTimeline's non-virtualized rendering no longer grows unboundedly — it's bounded to ~500 DOM rows per open channel/tab instead of growing forever for the life of the session. This resolves the critical unbounded-memory-leak aspect.

True virtualization (windowing so only visible rows + overscan are mounted) is still worth doing for rendering/scroll performance with large channels (500 rows x N open tabs x images/ResizeObservers per row is still non-trivial), but it requires reimplementing scroll-to-bottom, roving focus, auto-scroll, live regions, and onReachTop against @mui/x-chat-headless's internals (StaticMessageListView), which carries real regression risk (see stored memory 'mui-xchat-bottom-anchor' about scroll-anchoring fragility in this component). Downgraded from P1 (memory leak) to P2 (performance follow-up) since the leak itself is fixed.

title: Reserve image space from metadata so late image loads stop shifting layout (5b)
description: Design: docs/design/2026-08-14-timeline-scroll-professionalism-design.md section 5b (milestone 3). Root cause F1: attachments render a tiny text placeholder until the image loads through the Electrobun RPC (api.getFileDataUrl), then MessageAttachments.tsx applies an aspect-ratio frame from useImageLoadInfo (up to 360px tall per .inline-image-frame CSS) - each image commit changes content height after initial render, which is what feeds pin loss and nondeterministic open position. The Mattermost API returns width/height but our MattermostFileInfo type in src/mainview/types.ts omits them. Fix: extend MattermostFileInfo with optional width/height; MessageAttachments renders the aspect-ratio frame immediately from metadata instead of waiting for load, with useImageLoadInfo remaining the fallback when metadata is absent; markdown-embedded images (no server metadata) get a bounded placeholder frame (fixed height <= 240px, consistent with the 360px max) so attachment shift is eliminated and markdown shift is capped. Verify the websocket/RPC normalization path actually populates width/height so the metadata is real, not just typed.
acceptance_criteria: Attachment frame renders aspect-ratio from metadata before image load resolves; harness pin-stability and open-at-bottom scenarios green (or measurably improved when combined with the keeper); focused bun tests for attachment rendering from metadata and fallback path pass; no regression in MuiMessageTimeline.test.tsx attachments coverage
close_reason: Implemented 5b image space reservation with tests and e2e verification

title: TimelineScrollKeeper: stick-to-bottom re-pin + settled open (5a+5d)
description: Design: docs/design/2026-08-14-timeline-scroll-professionalism-design.md section 5a+5d (milestone 2). Symptoms: (1) after scrolling to bottom and idling ~2s, late layout shift (image load, late avatar, reaction pill, code-block font metrics) pushes the viewport up a few messages because @mui/x-chat-headless useMessageListBehavior only re-pins to bottom while streaming and Antimatter never streams; (2) opening a chat lands a nondeterministic distance above the bottom because the fire-twice scrollToBottom effect (sync + rAF) in MuiMessageTimeline.tsx ~line 194 runs before late commits change height, with nothing to correct after. Fix: new TimelineScrollKeeper component rendered via MessageList.Root overlay slot (the only app-reachable spot inside MessageListContextProvider). Reads isAtBottom + scrollToBottom from useMessageListContext(); attaches a ResizeObserver to .mui-message-list-content (located via closest('.mui-message-list-root') from the overlay element); on any content-height change while isAtBottom is true, calls scrollToBottom(). Generalizes the library streaming-only re-pin into Discord/Slack follow-the-bottom behavior; goes inert the moment the user scrolls beyond the 96px buffer. Settled open (5d): on channel switch/open set stick=true, re-pin on each content ResizeObserver tick until content height is stable for 200ms (bounded ~2s total), then release to normal keeper behavior. Preserves existing loadMoreReadyChannelId gating; the stick window subsumes the double-rAF hack; simplify the existing channel-switch effect so keeper owns stay semantics and the effect owns channel-switch only. Fallback if the overlay slot misbehaves: portal into the scroller parent from app root.
acceptance_criteria: Harness scenario 1 (pin stability) and scenario 2 (open-at-bottom) specs green; existing bun test src/mainview/components/mui-headless-timeline/MuiMessageTimeline.test.tsx passes; keeper renders inert under server-render (no DOM measurement crashes); no scroll coercion while user is scrolled up
notes: Implemented 2026-08-14. New: src/mainview/components/mui-headless-timeline/TimelineScrollKeeper.tsx (+ .test.tsx, 10 unit tests) rendered via MessageList.Root overlay slot; MuiMessageTimeline.tsx channel-switch effect simplified to the single initial pin (rAF double-scroll removed, loadMoreReadyChannelId gating preserved). e2e: added scenario 1b (no coercion while reading history). KEY FINDINGS: (1) native scroll anchoring is load-bearing for parked readers - scenario 1b asserts on the visible row, not scrollTop; (2) anchoring scroll events fire BEFORE RO callbacks and engines differ on visibility of the adjustment - the keeper tracks wasAtBottom in its own scroll listener, skipping events whose scrollHeight no longer matches the last observed content height (anchoring artifact vs user intent); (3) a pin trails its commit by one frame (16-20ms) - scenario 1 asserts no sustained streak >150ms above the 96px buffer + final distance <=96, not a max over samples. Results (all green, stable across 5 webkit + 2 chromium full runs): scenario 1 worst streak 19-20ms webkit / 5ms chromium, final distance 0; scenario 2 fully in view distance 0 (was 1549px below); scenario 1b same visible row 0.2px shift; scenario 3 drift 0.0 unchanged. Unit 259 pass / 0 fail; typecheck 0 errors; biome clean. server.ts gained E2E_NO_MINIFY flag (debugging aid).
close_reason: TimelineScrollKeeper shipped via overlay slot with settle-window open semantics; scenarios 1, 1b, 2, 3 green on webkit and chromium with numbers recorded in the design doc (5a/5d STATUS blocks + engine findings for 5c).

title: E2E timeline harness + red specs for the three scroll defects
description: Design: docs/design/2026-08-14-timeline-scroll-professionalism-design.md sections 3-4 (milestone 1 of the implementation order). Bun test server-renders only, so no scroll behavior is ever exercised today; this harness is the evidence base and regression net for every scroll fix that follows. Build: tests/e2e/harness/{harness.tsx,index.html,fixture.ts,api.ts} mounting the real MuiMessageTimeline standalone with chatDataStore seeded like MuiMessageTimeline.test.tsx and resolveImageSrc stubbed with configurable latency returning generated SVG data URLs of exact dimensions; tests/e2e/server.ts bun static server with the page bundled via bun build; playwright.config + specs with project safari (system WebKit, no browser download) as primary and chromium cross-check; package.json devDependency @playwright/test (no browser download) and script test:e2e (local/dev-only, NOT CI). window.__harness control API: openChannel/loadMore (through the real onLoadMore prop)/appendMessages/settle/getScrollTrace (rAF-sampled scrollTop/scrollHeight/clientHeight time series + scroll-event counter). Black-screen detection via per-scenario screenshot of the timeline rect downsampled and scored for pixel uniformity. Write the three acceptance specs red on current code: (1) pin stability: open channel with image-bearing history, scroll to bottom, settle() images, wait 3s idle, assert scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop <= 96 for the whole trace tail; (2) open-at-bottom: 300 messages 30% images, last message fully in view within 1s of posts arriving and stays through image settle; (3) load-more integrity: onReachTop with ~400ms latency then immediate downward wheel scroll through the prepended region, assert anchor drift <= 24px, no uniform-dark screenshot region, no telemetry frame stall > 150ms, no eager second page load.
acceptance_criteria: bun run test:e2e runs on system WebKit; the three scenario specs execute and are RED (fail) against current main; harness page mounts the real MuiMessageTimeline with deterministic fixtures and stubbed image latency; no changes to production timeline code in this milestone
notes: Implemented and measured 2026-08-14. title: notifications sometimes don't get delivered until the app is focused
notes:
[stab] Disabled macOS App Nap to address burst-on-focus.

Root cause: the live WebSocket runs in the bun process (src/bun/index.ts:785), not the renderer. The mainview MattermostWebSocketClient is dead code (nothing imports it). When the app is backgrounded, macOS App Nap suspends the bun process timers, deferring bun-to-mainview forwarding of WS events until focus returns, producing a burst of notifications on focus.

Fix:
- scripts/disable-app-nap.ts sets NSAppNapDisabled=true on built app bundles via /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy (idempotent). Unit-tested against a temp bundle (3 tests).
- Wired as top-level scripts.postWrap in electrobun.config.ts. Verified to fire during a packaged build: the canary build log shows the postWrap script running and the freshly-built bundle has NSAppNapDisabled=true.

Gates: typecheck clean, bun test 75/75.

PENDING: manual runtime verification. Run a packaged build, background the app, send messages, and confirm prompt delivery instead of a burst. If App-Nap disable proves insufficient (for example fully-occluded-window WKWebView timer throttling), the next step is an NSProcessInfo beginActivity runtime assertion from the bun process.
Completed the renderer->bun log bridge so the full notification pipeline lands in ONE log file for a packaged (backgrounded) run.

DONE this session:
- New src/mainview/app/rendererLog.ts (pure rendererLogVia(send,tag,args,now) -> {line}) + unit test (3 tests). Kept import-free of heavy frameworks so its test doesn't load the editor/view runtime (same lesson as the mention-helper extraction).
- Wired end-to-end: bun handles bun.messages.rendererLog (appendLogLine verbatim, try/catch); rpc.ts exports rendererLog(tag,...args) bound to electrobun.rpc.send.rendererLog; replaced the 8 renderer console.log('[Renderer]'/'[Notification]') call sites in rpc.ts + useMainViewEvents.ts with rendererLog(...). Dropped performance.now() (process-relative, not comparable across processes) in favor of the ISO Date.now() that formatLogLine already emits.
- Removed dead code in src/bun/index.ts: unused logFile const + now-unused join/LOG_FILENAME imports.

VERIFIED:
- typecheck clean; bun test 82/82 (was 75: +4 logger, +3 rendererLog).
- electrobun build succeeds.
- Ran the freshly-built dev bundle; confirmed the tee writes ~/Library/Logs/antimatter.ericschmar.dev/<channel>/antimatter.log with [session]/[log] [RPC]/[log] [WS] lines and ISO timestamps. Renderer [renderer]/[Notification] lines are appended verbatim (no double-tag) once a post event flows.

CLARIFICATION (not a regression): electrobun only runs scripts.postWrap for canary/stable builds (cli/index.ts line 3738 'if (buildEnvironment !== "dev")' gates the wrap stage that calls runHook('postWrap')). So the dev bundle correctly lacks NSAppNapDisabled; the canary bundle has NSAppNapDisabled=true (verified). App-Nap-disable fix is intact for the env that matters.

PENDING (needs a human at the keyboard): build canary (bun run build:canary), launch the bundle, background the app, have someone send you a message, then inspect the log file. If [WS] Message received timestamps arrive within ~1s of the server send and [log] [Notification] Fired by bun follows promptly -> App-Nap disable is sufficient. If [WS] timestamps cluster at refocus -> still throttled; fall back to an NSProcessInfo beginActivity runtime assertion from the bun process. Log path + grep: tail -f ~/Library/Logs/antimatter.ericschmar.dev/canary/antimatter.log | grep -E 'WS|RPC|Notification|session'.
close_reason: Closed

title: new messages in timeline cause reactions to disappear and reappear
notes:
ROOT CAUSE: Reactions live in state.posts[id].metadata.reactions (loaded via loadPostReactions), but selectedChannelHistory.posts never carries them. Every incoming WebSocket post calls mutateSelectedChannelHistory(addPostToHistory), creating a new selectedChannelHistory reference, which re-triggered the channel-history sync effect. That effect wholesale-replaced state.posts with the reaction-less history posts (reactions disappear), then async-refetched reactions for ALL posts (reactions reappear) — a visible flicker on every new message.

FIX: Added pure helper applyChannelHistory(state, history) in src/mainview/utils/state.ts that re-seeds posts/postOrder from history but carries over already-loaded metadata.reactions from existing state. The sync effect in MainViewApp now uses it, and only calls loadPostReactions for posts that don't already have reactions. Covered by new unit tests in state.test.ts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Single scroll anchoring authority: overflow-anchor none on the scroller (5c)
description: Design: docs/design/2026-08-14-timeline-scroll-professionalism-design.md section 5c (milestone 4). Root cause F3: three mechanisms fight over scrollTop - WebKit native scroll anchoring (overflow-anchor default), the library captureAnchor/restoreAnchor compensation on prepend and resize, and our app-level scrollToBottom effect. During load-more a prepend is classified by classifyItemChange and restoreAnchor runs in a layout effect; if WebKit already did its own anchor adjustment on the same mutation the compensations double-apply, visible as drift, jump, or the black-flash when the scroller paint is invalidated mid-compensation. Fix: add overflow-anchor: none to .mui-message-list-scroller in MuiMessageTimeline.css. Strictly measured keep-or-drop: run harness scenario 3 (load-more integrity) before and after on the Safari project; keep only if strictly better or neutral; if it regresses, drop it and record the measurement and reasoning in the design doc section 5c.
acceptance_criteria: Harness scenario 3 anchor-drift number recorded before and after on WebKit; change kept only if better-or-neutral; measurement + decision recorded in the 2026-08-14 design doc; bunx @biomejs/biome check passes on the CSS file (no !important)
close_reason: Kept overflow-anchor none after neutral/slightly better WebKit scenario 3 measurement
